Judge whether the copy matches the brand voice.

Subject: The Beacon headlamp is here — 400 lumens, 40 hours, 95 grams
Preview: New lighting technology built for the trail. USB-C rechargeable, ready when you are.
Body: You know what it's like when your headlamp starts to dim three miles from the trailhead. The Beacon was built so that doesn't happen.

The Northbay Beacon Headlamp puts out 400 lumens — enough to read terrain clearly at a solid pace on a dark trail. It runs up to 40 hours on a single charge, so a multi-day trip doesn't mean rationing light. When you do need to top it off, it charges via USB-C, the same cable you're probably already carrying.

At 95 grams, it won't shift your pack balance or fatigue your neck on long days. The Beacon is a capable headlamp for backpacking, camp chores, and trail running. It is not designed for technical cave exploration or high-output rescue work — if that's your use case, you'll want something spec'd for it.

Revolutionary new lighting technology. Practical weight. Real runtime. That's the Beacon.
Score 0-1; a score below 0.75 is a fail.
